clue.text: Once developed, photos of their home oddly tell it like it is

indicators.note: photos are developed into prints, and here the letters are developed into a new arrangement
oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters (first and third) of home

explanation.surface: Photographs of a family house, once printed, reveal the plain truth about its owners.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes PHOTOS, OF, THEIR and HM (the odd letters of 'home').
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for speaking bluntly and directly, without careful preparation or tact.

clue.text: Seafood special briefly cooked in local? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: in on its own would put the special inside the local
this reverses the stated containment, so the cooked local goes inside the special instead

parts.note: SP is a standard abbreviation for special

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of local are prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub's seafood special, cooked on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like the pub where the food is cooked; 'Just the opposite!' tells you the container and contents swap roles from the way 'in' first reads.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a bivalve shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Without money in April, maybe I will be very busy

indicators.note: without signals that the letter for money is dropped from the month

parts.note: April is an example of a month
the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: Someone broke in April expects to be rushing around working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'April, maybe' is the month itself, not a definition by example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: constantly active and moving about, with no time to rest.

clue.text: Novel representation of a Royal deanship?

wordplay.reading: ROY AL DEAN in a SHIP

parts.note: split the run as Roy, Al and Dean, three men's names, followed by ship, a boat

explanation.surface: A question about how a royal dean's office might be depicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal deanship' looks like a single title, but it splits into three male names, Roy, Al and Dean, then 'ship', a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic book about a Thames boating holiday is a famous novel.

clue.text: Determined to decipher old verse

indicators.note: deciphering works out a jumble, so the letters of old verse are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to work out the meaning of an ancient poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone firmly set on a course is determined or decided.

clue.text: Mother's offspring becoming secret society members

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
sons are offspring

explanation.surface: A mother's children grow up to join a secretive brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons belong to a fraternal order famous for secret rites.

clue.text: Revolutionary French bury link with English inside adventure story

indicators.note: inside puts the letter for English within the rearranged letters
revolutionary means overturned, so the letters of French bury link are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: French revolutionaries burying a connection with an Englishman somewhere in the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary French' looks like a description of people, but 'Revolutionary' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's novel follows a boy rafting down the Mississippi, a classic adventure tale.

clue.text: Hard yet malleable? Add water

indicators.note: something malleable can be reshaped, so the letters of hard yet are reformed

explanation.surface: Clay that is hard yet workable needs a splash of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydrate something is to supply it with moisture, combining it with or soaking it in liquid.

clue.text: Quietly send another message by way of excuse

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to retext is to send a text message again

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly fires off a further message to make an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a false reason given to cover a real motive is an excuse.

clue.text: When tense skier stumbles, beginning to see stars

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: a stumble throws the skier's letters out of order
beginning to asks for the first letter of see

explanation.surface: A nervous skier falls and sees stars from the knock.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbols * are called stars in everyday speech.

clue.text: Revolutionary group looked after Democrat's advancement

indicators.note: advancement means the letter for Democrat is moved forward in the word

parts.note: cared means looked after
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A political group that supported a Democrat's rise to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advancement' moves the D of CARED two places earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core unit of activists, especially in a communist or revolutionary party.

clue.text: Subject of Belgian city

definitions.meaning: in feudal use a vassal owing allegiance to a lord
a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse

explanation.surface: The topic is a city in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a feudal subject or vassal, and is also the name of a Walloon city.

clue.text: During WW2 US help tennis star needing rest

parts.note: Ivan Lendl was a world number one tennis player of the 1980s
ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A tennis star in wartime America needing a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1941 American programme supplying war materials to Britain and allies is the help described.

clue.text: Wards for the elderly generally encourage socialising in the first instance

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: this takes the initial letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: Care homes for older people tend to encourage mixing from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wards' suggests hospital rooms, but here it means people under someone's protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Protégés are people guided and protected by a patron, as wards are by guardians.

clue.text: A whatsit with its top missing is worthless

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, so the leading letter is removed

parts.note: a whatsit is an unnamed thing or object

explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something wretched and contemptible, of the lowest possible value.

clue.text: Youth's silence constraining unknown amateur entertainer

indicators.note: constraining means holding within, so the unknown goes inside the pair

parts.note: a lad is a youth
to gag is to silence
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A young person's being hushed holds back a nameless amateur performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The American pop singer known for theatrical shows is a famous entertainer.

clue.text: Manoeuvre of switching parts in signalling system

indicators.note: switching the two halves round swaps the first three letters with the last three

parts.note: tic-tac is the hand-signal code used by British racecourse bookmakers

explanation.surface: Changing components inside a signalling network as a planned move.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the arm-waving code bookies at British racecourses use to pass on odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move or ploy to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Slices head off fish to get lean cut

parts.note: to top something is to cut off its top, so this is tops
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A cook beheads a fish to prepare a lean cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef from the upper hindquarter.

clue.text: Worry about money almost brings ruin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worry goes round the shortened money

parts.note: care means worry

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Anxiety over finances nearly leads to financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcase is the bare shell or remains of a ruined building or body.

clue.text: Housing motorists in old boats

indicators.note: in places the motorists inside the old boats

parts.note: barks are an old word for sailing ships
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Drivers being given accommodation in antique boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: soldiers' accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings in which soldiers are lodged.

clue.text: Blackbird's a flier?

parts.note: a bird whose name starts with a black fuel, coal, then tit, a small bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blackbird' suggests the thrush; here it is a black-named bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small European songbird has a black cap, and its name joins a black mineral to a bird.

clue.text: Dons scrapped over year in charge of church council

indicators.note: over means covering, so the rearranged dons go round the year
scrapped suggests the word dons is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: University dons argued over a year while running a church assembly.

clue.text: Type of dance jacket

definitions.meaning: a Spanish dance in triple time
a short open jacket ending above the waist

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Spanish dance in triple time and a short open jacket.

clue.text: Arty group writhing in intense discomfort

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters of arty group are twisted

explanation.surface: A group of arty types squirming in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, purgatory is a state of great suffering, from the place of torment in Catholic belief.

clue.text: Long, long time before end of recession

parts.note: a year is a long time

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of recession

explanation.surface: Wishing for a long time for a slump to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective repeated; the first is the verb, meaning to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to long for something is to ache with desire for it.

clue.text: On reflection monogamist enjoys a perfect state

enjoys means possesses, so the word monogamist holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a faithful partner finds bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists call the final adult stage of an insect its perfect state.

clue.text: Set free with loss of name and power, simply wasted away

indicators.note: loss means the letters for name and power are taken out

parts.note: emancipated means set free

explanation.surface: Someone freed but stripped of identity and strength simply withers away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone emaciated has become abnormally thin and weak through hunger or illness.

clue.text: Choose eccentric German to initially implement curriculum of branch of science

parts.note: to elect is to choose

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre, so the letters of German to are disordered
initially asks for the first letters of implement and curriculum

explanation.surface: Pick an eccentric German to roll out a science curriculum.
